hits.title: On the chromatic number of real and rational spaces
hits.text:
Summary: The chromatic number of a space is the minimum number of colors with which the whole space can be colored so that no two points of the same color are at unit distance.

We prove that the chromatic number of the six-dimensional real Euclidean space, \(\mathbb R^6\), is at least 11. In addition we give a new proof of the lower bound 9 for the chromatic number of \(\mathbb R^5\). We also simplify the proof of the lower bound 7 for \(\mathbb R^4\).

We improve the lower bounds on the chromatic number of five-dimensional and seven-dimensional rational space to 8 and 15, respectively.

hits.title: On rational analogs of Nelson-Hadwiger's and Borsuk's problems
hits.text: Summary: In this paper, we consider affine-rational analogs of Nelson-Hadwiger problem on finding the chromatic number of the rational space and Borsuk's problem on partitioning into parts of smaller diameter. New lower bounds are proved. In particular, bounds on the minimum dimension of a counterexample to Borsuk's conjecture are found.

hits.title: On 4-chromatic subgraphs of \(G(\mathbb Q^3,d)\)
hits.text: Summary: We address the chromatic number of a class of Euclidean distance graphs having vertex set \(\mathbb Q^3\), the 3-dimensional rational space. It is shown that if \(s\) is any positive integer with no prime factors congruent to \(2\pmod{3}\), and \(G\) is the graph with vertex set \(\mathbb Q^3\) where any two vertices are adjacent if and only if they are distance \(\sqrt{2s}\) apart, then \(G\) has chromatic number 4. Along the way, we obtain a few results on the chromatic numbers of certain Euclidean distance graphs having vertex set \(\mathbb Z^3\), the 3-dimensional integer space. We conclude by constructing an example (possibly the first) of a triangle-free, 4-chromatic distance graph in \(\mathbb Q^3\).

hits.text: Let \(Q^{n}\) be the \(n\)-dimensional rational space with the Euclidean metric. The chromatic number \(\chi (Q^{n})\) is the smallest numbers of colors needed to color all points of \(Q^{n}\) such that no points at the distance \(1\) are assigned the same color. It has been known that \(\chi (Q^{n})\geq (1.173...+o(1))^{n}.\) In this note the authors announce an improved lower bound \(\chi (Q^{n})\geq (1.199...+o(1))^{n}.\) Only a sketch of the proof is provided.

hits.title: More on the second Babai number and second clique number of \(\mathbb Q^3\)
hits.text: Let \({\mathbb{Q}}^3 \) be the three-dimensional rational space. In graph \(G({\mathbb{Q}}^3,\{d_1,d_2\})\) two vertices are adjacent if their Euclidean distance is equal to \(d_1\) or \(d_2\) where \(d_1\) and \(d_2\) are positive real numbers. The maximal chromatic number of \(G({\mathbb{Q}}^3,\{d_1,d_2\})\) is called the second Babai number and denoted as \(B_2({\mathbb{Q}}^3)\). The second clique number is the maximal clique number of \(G({\mathbb{Q}}^3,\{d_1,d_2\})\) and denoted as \(C_2({\mathbb{Q}}^3)\). In the paper it is proved that \(C_2({\mathbb{Q}}^3) = 6\) and \(B_2({\mathbb{Q}}^3) \geq 6\).

hits.title: A new lower bound for the chromatic number of the rational space
hits.source: Russ. Math. Surv. 68, No. 5, 960-962 (2013); translation from Usp. Mat. Nauk 68, No. 5, 183-184 (2013).
hits.text: Let \(Q^{n}\) be the \(n\)-dimensional rational space with the Euclidean metric. The chromatic number \(\chi (Q^{n})\) is the smallest numbers of colors needed to color all points of \(Q^{n}\) such that no points at the distance \(1\) are assigned the same color. It has been known that \(\chi (Q^{n})\geq (1.173...+o(1))^{n}.\) In this note the authors announce an improved lower bound \(\chi (Q^{n})\geq (1.199...+o(1))^{n}.\) Only a sketch of the proof is provided.

hits.title: Sharp extensions of Bernstein's inequality to rational spaces
hits.text:
Sharp extensions of some classical polynomial inequalities of Bernstein are established for rational function spaces on the unit circle, on \(K=\mathbb{R}\pmod{2\pi}\), on \([-1,1]\) and on \(\mathbb{R}\). The key result is the establishment of the inequality 
\[
|f'(z_0)|\leq\max \Biggl\{\sum_{\substack{ j=1\\ |a_j|>1}}^n{|a_j|^2-1\over|a_j-z_0|^2},\;\sum_{\substack{ j=1\\ |a_j|<1}}^n {1-|a_j|^2\over|a_j-z_0|^2}\Biggr\}|f|_{\partial D}
\]
 for every rational function \(f=p_n/q_n\), where \(p_n\) is a polynomial of degree at most \(n\) with complex coefficients and 
\[
q_n(z)= \prod^n_{j=1} (z-a_j)
\]
 with \(|a_j|\neq 1\) for each \(j\), and for every \(z_0\in\partial D\), where \(\partial D-\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|=1\}\). The above inequality is sharp at every \(z_0\in\partial D\).

hits.title: The Beckman-Quarles theorem for rational spaces
hits.text: The Beckmann-Quarles theorem asserts that for \(d > 1\) every mapping from a \(d\)-dimensional real space \(R^d\) into itself preserving the unit distance (`unit-preserving', i.e. pairs of points with distance 1 will be mapped into pairs of points, again with distance 1) will preserve any distance and hence is an isometry. For the rational case \(Q^d\) the same proposition is not a foregone conclusion. For some numbers \(d\) the matter has already been settled; the author adds the proof for the case of dimensions \(d = 2 n^2-1\) for \(n > 2\). This proof is indeed versatile as it can also be applied to several other cases.

hits.title: Universal rational spaces
hits.text: All spaces considered are totally bounded metric spaces. The rim-type of a space is the smallest ordinal \(\alpha\) such that there is a basis for the open sets with boundaries whose \(\alpha\)-th derivatives are empty. The \(\alpha\)-th derivative \(A^{(\alpha)}\) of a set A is defined inductively as follows: \(A^{(0)}=A\), \(A^{(\alpha +1)}\) is the set of the limit points of \(A^{(\alpha)}\), and if \(\alpha\) is a limit ordinal, \(A^{(\alpha)}=\cap \{A^{(\beta)}| \quad \beta <\alpha \}.\) A containing space for a class \({\mathcal C}\) of spaces is a space X such that each space in \({\mathcal C}\) can be embedded in X. If in addition \(X\in {\mathcal C}\), then X is called a universal space for \({\mathcal C}\). The authors investigate the existence of containing spaces and universal spaces for certain classes of spaces, especially for spaces of rim-type \(\leq \alpha\), rational spaces, and one-dimensional spaces. The techniques involve sequences of partitions of the sort used by \textit{Anderson} in his characterization of Menger's universal curve.

hits.title: A proof of Ganea's conjecture for rational spaces
hits.text: Ganea's conjecture concerns the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of spaces. It is easy to show that \(cat(S\times T)\leq cat(S)+cat(T)\). Both strict inequality and equality can occur, but the only known examples of strict inequality appear when S and T have homology torsion. This led Ganea to the conjecture that \(cat(T\times S^ n)=cat(T)+1\) for every finite complex T and \(n\geq 1\). The author gives a proof of Ganea's conjecture whenever T is a rational simply connected space and \(n\geq 2\). The proof uses Sullivan's minimal models. If (\(\Lambda\) X,d) denotes the minimal model of a space S, then \(cat_ 0(S)\), resp. \(Mcat_ 0(S)\), is the least integer n such that the minimal model of the projection \((\Lambda X,d)\to (\Lambda X,\Lambda^{>n}x,T)\) admits a retraction as differential graded algebra, resp. as differential graded (\(\Lambda\) X,d)-module. If S is a rational space, then \(cat(S)=cat_ 0(S)\). In general, \(cat_ 0(S)\leq cat(S)\). The first step in the proof is due to B. Jessup \((Mcat_ 0(S)+1=Mcat_ 0(S\times S^ n)),\) the second step, the main part of this paper, consists of proving that \(Mcat_ 0(S)=cat_ 0(S)\).

hits.title: Chebyshev polynomials and Markov-Bernstein type inequalities for rational spaces
hits.source: J. Lond. Math. Soc., II. Ser. 50, No. 3, 501-519 (1994).
hits.text:
Chebyshev ``polynomials'' for the rational function spaces 
\[
{\mathcal T}_ n (a_ 1, a_ 2, \dots, a_ n):= \Biggl\{ {{t(\theta)} \over {\prod^ n_{k=1} | a_ k- \cos \theta|}}:\;t\in {\mathcal T}_ n \Biggr\}
\]
 are explicitly found, where \({\mathcal T}_ n\) denotes the set of all trigonometric polynomials of degree at most \(n\) with real coefficients, and where \(\{a_ 1, a_ 2,\dots, a_ n\} \subset \mathbb{C} \setminus [-1, 1]\) is a fixed set. 


Chebyshev ``polynomials'' of the first and second kinds for the corresponding algebraic rational function spaces are also studied as well as orthogonal ``polynomials'' with respect to the weight function \((1- x^ 2 )^{-1/2}\) on \([-1, 1]\). Several explicit expressions for these ``polynomials'' are obtained. As a beautiful application, an extension of the classical Bernstein-Szegő inequality is proved. It states that 
\[
f' (\theta)^ 2+ B_ n (\theta)^ 2 f(\theta)^ 2\leq B_ n (\theta)^ 2 \max_{\tau\in \mathbb{R}} | f(\tau)|^ 2
\]
 for every \(f\in {\mathcal T}_ n (a_ 1, a_ 2, \dots, a_ n)\) and \(\theta\in \mathbb{R}\), where 
\[
B_ n (\theta):= \text{Re} \Biggl( \sum_{k=1}^ n {{\sqrt {a^ 2_ k-1}} \over {a_ k- \cos \theta}} \Biggr)
\]
 with the choice of \(\sqrt {a^ 2_ k-1}\) determined by \(| a_ k- \sqrt {a^ 2_ k -1} |<1\). This contains the classical Bernstein-Szegő inequality as a limiting case.

hits.title: On the chromatic number of some rational spaces
hits.text: Let \(Q^ d\) be the set of all the rational points of the euclidean \(d\)- space, and let \(G(Q^ d)\) be the graph whose vertex-set is \(Q^ d\), where two points are adjacent if they are at distance one. It was shown in \textit{D. R. Woodall} [J. Comb. Theory, Ser. A 14, 187-200 (1973; Zbl 0251.50003)] that \(\chi(G(Q^ 2))=2\), in \textit{M. Benda} and \textit{M. Perles} [Colorings of metric spaces (unpublished)] that \(\chi(G(Q^ 3))=2\) and \(\chi(G(Q^ 4))=4\), and in the author's paper [Aequationes Math. 37, No. 2/3, 259-266 (1989; Zbl 0705.05033)] that \(\chi(G(Q^ 5))\geq 4\), \(\chi(G(Q^ 6))\geq 6\), \(\chi(G(Q^ 7))\geq 8\) and \(\chi(G(Q^ 8))\geq 9\). In the paper under review, the author improves his previous result by raising each of his four lower bounds by one.

hits.title: On spherically generated rational spaces
hits.source: Behara, Minaketan (ed.) et al., Proceedings of the 2nd Gauss symposium. Conference A: Mathematics and theoretical physics, Munich, Germany, August 2-7, 1993. Berlin: Walter de Gruyter. Symposia Gaussiana, 491-498 (1995).
hits.text:
A description is given of \(\ker h^*: H^*(X,Q) \to \pi^*(X,Q)\), where \(h^*\) is the dual Hurewicz homomorphism, in terms of the \(A (\infty)\)-algebra structure on \(H^*(X;Q)\). More precisely, the author proves that \(X\) is spherically generated if and only if the \(A(\infty)\)-indecomposables of \(H^*(X;Q)\) coincide with the usual indecomposables. This result can be rephrased in other terms. It says that \(X\) is spherically generated if and only if the indecomposables of \(H^*(X;Q)\) are represented by generators in the Sullivan minimal model of \(X\), or if and only if all the matrix Massey products are represented by decomposable elements.

For the entire collection see [Zbl 0828.00029].

hits.title: A discrete form of the Beckman-Quarles theorem for rational spaces
hits.text:
Let \(A=\{4k(k+1):k=1,2,3,\dots \} \cup (\{k^2: k=1,2,3,\dots \} \cap \{2k^2-1: k=2,3,4,\dots \})\). The author proves: if \(n \in A\) and \(x,y \in \mathbb Q^n\), then there exists a finite set \(\{x,y\} \subseteq S_{xy} \subseteq \mathbb Q^n\) such that for every unit-distance preserving mapping \(f:S_{xy} \to \mathbb Q^n\), \(\|f(x)-f(y)\|=\|x-y\|\) holds. 


The theorem for \(n=8\) was earlier proved by \textit{A. Tyszka} [Aequationes Math. 62, No. 1-2, 85-93 (2001; Zbl 1004.51023)].

hits.title: Compactifications with minimum rim-types of rational spaces
hits.text: In a previous paper, the second author stated that the separable metric spaces which admit rational compactifications are exactly those spaces which have a basis of open sets with scattered boundaries. (A space is rational if it has a basis of open sets with countable boundaries.) The purpose of the current paper is to fill a gap in the proof of the earlier theorem by proving a stronger result. For every space \(A\), let \(A^{(0)} = A\), let \(A^{(1)}\) be the set of limit points of \(A\), and for an ordinal \(\alpha\), let \(A^{(\alpha)} = (A^{(\alpha-1)})^{(1)}\) if \(\alpha\) is a successor ordinal, and \(A^{(\alpha)} = \bigcap\{A^{(\beta)}: \beta < \alpha\}\) if \(\alpha\) is a limit ordinal. \(A\) has type \(\alpha\) if \(\alpha\) is the smallest ordinal for which \(A^{(\alpha)} = \emptyset\). A space has rim-type \(\leq \alpha\) iff it has a basis of open sets whose boundaries have type \(\leq \alpha\). The main result of this paper is that a separable metric space of rim-type \(\leq \alpha + n\) (where \(\alpha\) is a limit ordinal and \(n\) is a non- negative integer) has a compactification of rim-type \(\leq \alpha + 2n + \min\{\alpha,1\}\).

hits.title: Rational spaces and the property of universality
hits.text: The main result of the paper is that the family of all metrizable rational spaces (i.e. spaces having countable basis of open sets with countable boundaries) has a universal space. Some interesting properties of the space are also proven and some questions are asked.

hits.title: On the chromatic number of real and rational spaces
hits.text:
Summary: The chromatic number of a space is the minimum number of colors with which the whole space can be colored so that no two points of the same color are at unit distance.

We prove that the chromatic number of the six-dimensional real Euclidean space, \(\mathbb R^6\), is at least 11. In addition we give a new proof of the lower bound 9 for the chromatic number of \(\mathbb R^5\). We also simplify the proof of the lower bound 7 for \(\mathbb R^4\).

We improve the lower bounds on the chromatic number of five-dimensional and seven-dimensional rational space to 8 and 15, respectively.

hits.title: Chromatic numbers of real and rational spaces with real or rational forbidden distances
hits.text: Summary: Several important aspects of the Nelson-Erdős-Hadwiger classical problem of combinatorial geometry are considered. In particular, new lower bounds are obtained for the chromatic numbers of the spaces \( \mathbb{R}^n\) and \( \mathbb{Q}^n\) with two, three or four forbidden distances.

hits.title: Rational spaces of a given rim-type and the property of universality
hits.text: Let all spaces be separable metric. A space X has rim-type \(\leq \alpha\), where \(\alpha\) is an ordinal number, if X has a base \({\mathcal B}\) such that the \(\alpha\) th derivative of the boundary of every element of \({\mathcal B}\) is empty. A space T is universal for a family \({\mathcal R}\) of spaces if every space in \({\mathcal R}\) can be imbedded in T and \(T\in {\mathcal R}\). A space T has the property of finite intersection with respect to a family \({\mathcal R}\) of spaces if for every \(X\in {\mathcal R}\) there is a fixed imbedding \(i_ X:\) \(X\to T\) such that for all different elements X,Y\(\in {\mathcal R}\), the set \(i_ X(X)\cap i_ Y(Y)\) is finite (it is not assumed that \(T\in {\mathcal R})\). Now let \({\mathcal T}_{\alpha}\) be the family of all spaces having rim-type \(\leq \alpha\). In this interesting paper the author proves that if \({\mathcal S}\) is a subfamily of \({\mathcal T}_{\alpha}\) of cardinality at most \({\mathfrak C}\), then there exists a space T which is universal for \({\mathcal T}_{\alpha}\) while moreover T has the property of finite intersection with respect to \({\mathcal S}\).

hits.title: Emergence of the Witt group in the cellular lattice of rational spaces
hits.text:
The \textit{closed class} generated by a pointed CW complex \(A\) is the smallest class \({\mathcal C}(A)\) of spaces which contains \(A\) and which is closed under (a) weak equivalences, and (b) pointed homotopy pushouts. The condition \(B\in {\mathcal C}(A)\) is denoted \(A\ll B\). This relation gives the category of spaces (with the homotopy type of a CW complex) a lattice structure, called the cellular lattice. It is known that the cellular lattice is highly nontrivial. The problem can be simplified somewhat by working rationally. This paper considers the sublattice of rationally formal spaces \(X\) that are \((6k-1)\)-dimensional, \((2k-1)\)-connected, and satisfy \(\pi_{2k}(X)\otimes \mathbb Q\neq 0\). The formality condition implies that the rational cellular type of such a space is determined by the differential \(\partial : {\mathbb L}_{4k-1} \to {\mathbb L}_{4k-2}\) in its Quillen model, which can be written \(\partial (y) = \sum c_{ij} [x_i,x_j]\), where \(\{ x_i\}\) is a basis for \({\mathbb L}_{2n-1}\). 


Let \({\mathbb M}\) denote the set of cellular classes of such spaces with the additional condition that there is at most one cell in dimension \(4k\). These cellular types are determined by the quadratic forms \(Q\) represented by the matrix of coefficients \(c_{ij}\). Quadratic forms fall into two classes: isotropic and anisotropic. The \textit{Witt ring} is the set of isometry classes of anisotropic forms; by passing to similarity classes one obtains a semigroup \(\overline {W({\mathbb Q})}\). 


The authors show that if \(Q\) is isotropic, then \(X\) is rationally cellularly equivalent to \(S^{2k}\). If \(X\) and \(Y\) are determined by anisotropic quadratic forms \(Q\) and \(Q'\), then \(Q\) and \(Q'\) are similar if and only if \(X\) and \(Y\) are cellularly equivalent. These results suffice to establish a bijection \({\mathbb M}\to \overline {W({\mathbb Q})}\); the authors go further and define a multiplication on \({\mathbb M}\) which makes this map a semigroup isomorphism.

hits.title: Lobatto-type quadrature formula in rational spaces
hits.text:
Let \({\mathcal P}_m\) be the set of all real algebraic polynomials of degree at most \(m\) and 
\[
{\mathcal P}_m(a_1, a_2,\dots, a_n)= \left\{{P(x) \over \prod^n_{k=1} | x-a_k |^2}, P\in{\mathcal P}_m \right\},
\]
 where the nonreal elements in \(\{a_k\}^n_{k=1} \subset\mathbb{C} \setminus[-1,1]\) are paired by complex conjugation. The author constructs the Lobatto-type quadrature formula 
\[
\int^1_{-1} {f(x)\over \sqrt{1-x^2}} dx\approx Q_n(f): =\lambda_0 f(1)+ \sum^{n-1}_{k=1} \lambda_k f(x_k)+ \lambda_n f(-1),
\]
 based on the \(n+1\) Chebyshev points \(-1=x_n< x_{n-1}< \cdots<x_1 <x_0=1\) such that \(T_n(x_k) =(-1)^k\), \(k=0,1, \dots,n\). He proves that it is a positive quadrature formula and it is exact for any element in \({\mathcal P}_{2n-1} (a_1,a_2, \dots,a_n)\). Moreover, a convergence result is given for \(f\in C[-1,1]\).

hits.title: Approximating rational spaces with elliptic complexes and conjecture of Anick
hits.text: Recall that a space is elliptic if its rational homotopy and rational homology are totally finite dimensional. All homogeneous spaces of compact Lie groups are elliptic, for example. While elliptic spaces are very special, some time ago, David Anick conjectured that every finite complex occurs as a skeleton of an elliptic complex. Following a suggestion of C. McGibbon, the authors of this paper turn the question into the homotopical one of approximating spaces by \(n\)-equivalences into or out of them. They take as their model the approximation of complexes by their skeleta or by the stages in their Postnikov towers. They first show that, for a class of spaces closed under taking skeleta and Postnikov sections, the ability to approximate each space in the class by maps into is equivalent to approximation by maps out of. Of course, when we say ``approximation'', we refer to an approximation by spaces coming from a chosen and fixed category. The authors then focus on a particular category \(\mathcal M\) of spaces which has proved to be useful in and amenable to rational homotopy theory. For this class of spaces, for which membership is defined in terms of the existence of a very special type of fibration, they show that approximations into by elliptic spaces may be made, implying that approximations out of by elliptic spaces also exist. Thus, the homotopical version of Anick's conjecture is verified for the class \(\mathcal M\).

hits.title: Rational spaces in resolving classes
hits.text:
Work of \textit{E. Dror Farjoun} [Cellular spaces, null spaces and homotopy localization. Berlin: Springer-Verlag (1995; Zbl 0842.55001)], \textit{W. Chachólski} [Prog. Math. 136, 95--118 (1996; Zbl 0856.55011)] and others in the 1990s established the basic theory of closed classes of spaces. Their work also demonstrated the utility of the `classes of spaces' point of view in generalizing and understanding classical theorems more deeply. For example, the Blakers-Massey excision theorem was shown by Chachólski to be a consequence of a cellular inequality involving the fibers of various maps in the diagram comparing a homotopy pushout square to a homotopy pullback square.

These classes and the relation \(\ll\) constitute a lattice, and it is natural to explore its structure and inquire as to how complicated it can be. Even among rational spaces there is a great deal of structure. For example, \textit{K. Hess} and \textit{P.-E. Parent} [Trans. Am. Math. Soc. 354, No. 11, 4571--4583 (2002; Zbl 1012.55015)] found sublattices isomorphic to a certain quotient of the Witt lattice of quadratic forms. A central tool used by Hess and Parent was a characterization of cellular inequalities between rational spaces: if \(X\) and \(Y\) are simply-connected rational spaces of finite type and the same connectivity, \(n-1\), then \(X \ll Y\) if and only if there is a map \(\bigvee X \to Y\) that is surjective on \(\pi_n\).

These ideas are ripe for dualization. In [Fundam. Math. 178, No. 2, 97--108 (2003; Zbl 1052.55015); ibid. 217, No. 2, 171--187 (2012; Zbl 1251.55010)], the reviewer defined a resolving class to be a nonempty class of (pointed) spaces that is closed under weak homotopy equivalence and homotopy limits. The smallest such class containing the space \(X\) is denoted \(\mathcal{R}(X)\), and the relation \(Y\in \mathcal{R}(X)\) is denoted \(X \prec Y\). There is then a lattice of resolving classes, and its structure is a natural thing to explore.

In the paper under review, the author carries out a program analogous to that of Hess and Parent. He provides a characterization of \(X \prec Y\) for rational spaces of finite type: if \(X\) and \(Y\) both have connectivity \(n-1\), then \(Y \prec X\) if and only if there is a map \(X \to \prod Y\) injective on \(\pi_n\). Using this, it is shown that the exact same quotient of the Witt lattice embeds into the lattice of resolving classes of rational spaces.

Interestingly, the algebra involved in the new result is very similar to the algebra Hess and Parent use, but it is not yet clear how to make a topological connection between the two embeddings. The paper concludes with an interesting list of further questions.

hits.title: On distance graphs in rational spaces
hits.source: Mosc. J. Comb. Number Theory 12, No. 2, 165-173 (2023).
hits.text: Let \(Q_n\) be the set of all positive definite rational quadratic forms on \(n\) variables. For any \(q\in Q_n\), let \(G(Q_n, q)\) denote the graph with vertex set \(Q_n\). Two vertices \(x, y \in Q_n\) are adjacent in the graph if and only if \(q(x - y) = 1\). This notion generalises standard Euclidean distance graphs. In this paper, the authors study these graphs and show how to find the exact value of the clique number of the graph \(G(Q_n, q)\). They also prove a rational analogue of the Beckman-Quarles theorem that any unit-preserving bijection of \(Q_n\) onto itself is an isometry.

hits.title: Asymptotic estimates for rational spaces on hypersurfaces in function fields
hits.text:
Let \(\mathbb F_q\) be a finite field of \(q\) elements, \(k:=\mathbb F_q(t)\), and \({\mathfrak o}:= \mathbb F_q[t]\). Let \(d(u)\) denote the degree of a polynomial \(u\) in \({\mathfrak o}\) and let 
\[
|\vec x|:= \max\{d(x_i)\mid 1\leq i\leq s\}
\]
 for \(\vec x=(x_1,\dots, x_s)\), \(\vec x\in{\mathfrak o}^*\). Let 
\[
H: \sum^s_{i=1} c_i z^l_i= 0
\]
 be a hypersurface defined over \(k\) (here \(c_i\in k\) for \(1\leq i\leq s\) and \(l\in\mathbb N\)). For \(\{X_1,\dots, X_m\}\subseteq k^s\), let \([X_1,\dots, X_m]\) denote the \(k\)-vector space spanned by the set of vectors \(\{X_1,\dots, X_m\}\). By a variant of the Hardy-Littlewood circle method, the author proves an asymptotic formula for the number 
\[
N(P):= \#\{(X_1,\dots, X_m)\mid\{X_1,\dots, X_m\}\subseteq{\mathfrak o}^s,\;[X_1,\dots, X_m]\subseteq H(k),|X_j|\leq P, 1\leq j\leq m\}
\]
 of \(m\)-tuples of vectors of bounded height generating a linear subspace of \(H(k)\), as \(P\to\infty\), and concludes that, under certain conditions on \(m\) and \(H\), the hypersurface \(H(k)\) contains infinitely many \(m\)-dimensional \(k\)-vector spaces.

hits.title: On the chromatic numbers of rational spaces
hits.source: Math. Notes 103, No. 1, 111-117 (2018); translation from Mat. Zametki 103, No. 1, 120-128 (2018).
hits.text:
The authors consider coloring problems similar to the well-known problem of determining the chromatic number of the plane. Given a rational number \(a\) and a positive integer \(n\), a rational \(a\)-distance graph in \(\mathbb{Q}^n\) is any graph whose vertices can be represented by points in \(\mathbb{Q}^n\) so that whenever two vertices are adjacent, the distance between the corresponding points in \(\mathbb{Q}^n\) is exactly \(a\). One can then define the chromatic number \(\chi(\mathbb{Q}^n)\) of the space \(\mathbb{Q}^n\) as the maximum value of \(\chi(G)\) over all graphs \(G\) such that \(G\) is a rational \(a\)-distance graph in \(\mathbb{Q}^n\) for some \(a \in \mathbb{Q}\). (In fact, it suffices to consider just \(a=1\).)

It was observed by \textit{E. I. Ponomarenko} and \textit{A. M. Raigorodskii} [``On the chromatic number of the space \(\mathbb{Q}^n\)'', Trudy Mosk. Fiz. Tekhn. Inst 4, No. 1, 127--130 (2012)] that often a graph which admits such a representation in \(\mathbb{Q}^n\) in fact admits coordinates which lie in some affine subspace of smaller dimension, albeit with non-rational coordinates inside subspace. Accordingly, the affine dimension of a graph \(G\), written \(\mathrm{affdim}(G)\), is defined to be the smallest \(n\) such that: the vertices of \(G\) can be assigned coordinates in an \(n\)-dimensional affine subspace of \(\mathbb{Q}^m\) for some \(m\) so that each pair of adjacent vertices has distance exactly \(1\) between the corresponding points. Analogous with the earlier definition, one then defines \(\chi_{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathbb{Q}^n)\) to be the maximum of \(\chi(G)\) over all rational \(1\)-distance graphs \(G\) with \(\mathrm{affdim}(G) \leq 1\). The author seeks techniques to give an upper bound on \(\chi_{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathbb{Q}^n)\), by relating this chromatic number to a similar type of chromatic number.

Say that a graph \(G\) whose vertices have coordinates in \(\mathbb{Q}^n\) is a \(\sqrt{Q}\)-graph if \(|x-y|^2\) is rational for all pairs of vertices \(x\) and \(y\), and say that \(G\) is a \(\sqrt{Q}\)-unit distance graph if additionally we have \(|x-y| = 1\) for every pair of adjacent vertices \(x,y\). The author then defines \(\chi_{\sqrt{Q}}(\mathbb{R}^n)\) as the maximum of \(\chi(G)\) over all \(\sqrt{Q}\)-unit distance graphs in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). The author proves the following main results concerning this parameter:
 {\parindent=8mm \begin{itemize}\item[(i)] \(\chi_{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathbb{Q}^n) = \chi_{\sqrt{Q}}(\mathbb{R}^n)\) for each positive integer \(n\),
 \item[(ii)] If \(G\) is a connected \(\sqrt{Q}\)-unit distance graph in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) containing a subgraph isomorphic to \(K_3\), then \(\chi(G) = 3\),
 \item[(iii)] If \(G\) is a connected \(\sqrt{Q}\)-unit distance graph in \(\mathbb{R}^3\) containing a subgraph isomorphic to \(K_4\), then \(\chi(G) = 4\),
 \item[(iv)] For every positive integer \(n\), \(\chi_{\sqrt{Q}}(\mathbb{R}^2) = \max\{ \chi(\mathbb{Q} \times \sqrt{q}\mathbb{Q}), q \in \mathbb{N}\}\). 


\end{itemize}} In light of the second and third theorems, which give upper bounds for what heuristically seem to be the ``worst-case graphs'' in their respective classes, the author poses the question of whether indeed \(\chi_{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathbb{Q}^2) = 3\) and \(\chi_{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathbb{Q}^3) = 4\). The author also asks whether analogs of these theorems hold in higher dimensions.

hits.text: Summary: Several important aspects of the Nelson-Erdős-Hadwiger classical problem of combinatorial geometry are considered. In particular, new lower bounds are obtained for the chromatic numbers of the spaces \( \mathbb{R}^n\) and \( \mathbb{Q}^n\) with two, three or four forbidden distances.

hits.title: On the chromatic number of real and rational spaces
hits.text:
Summary: The chromatic number of a space is the minimum number of colors with which the whole space can be colored so that no two points of the same color are at unit distance.

We prove that the chromatic number of the six-dimensional real Euclidean space, \(\mathbb R^6\), is at least 11. In addition we give a new proof of the lower bound 9 for the chromatic number of \(\mathbb R^5\). We also simplify the proof of the lower bound 7 for \(\mathbb R^4\).

We improve the lower bounds on the chromatic number of five-dimensional and seven-dimensional rational space to 8 and 15, respectively.

hits.title: On rational analogs of Nelson-Hadwiger's and Borsuk's problems
hits.text: Summary: In this paper, we consider affine-rational analogs of Nelson-Hadwiger problem on finding the chromatic number of the rational space and Borsuk's problem on partitioning into parts of smaller diameter. New lower bounds are proved. In particular, bounds on the minimum dimension of a counterexample to Borsuk's conjecture are found.

hits.title: A new lower bound for the chromatic number of the rational space
hits.source: Russ. Math. Surv. 68, No. 5, 960-962 (2013); translation from Usp. Mat. Nauk 68, No. 5, 183-184 (2013).
hits.text: Let \(Q^{n}\) be the \(n\)-dimensional rational space with the Euclidean metric. The chromatic number \(\chi (Q^{n})\) is the smallest numbers of colors needed to color all points of \(Q^{n}\) such that no points at the distance \(1\) are assigned the same color. It has been known that \(\chi (Q^{n})\geq (1.173...+o(1))^{n}.\) In this note the authors announce an improved lower bound \(\chi (Q^{n})\geq (1.199...+o(1))^{n}.\) Only a sketch of the proof is provided.

hits.title: On 4-chromatic subgraphs of \(G(\mathbb Q^3,d)\)
hits.text: Summary: We address the chromatic number of a class of Euclidean distance graphs having vertex set \(\mathbb Q^3\), the 3-dimensional rational space. It is shown that if \(s\) is any positive integer with no prime factors congruent to \(2\pmod{3}\), and \(G\) is the graph with vertex set \(\mathbb Q^3\) where any two vertices are adjacent if and only if they are distance \(\sqrt{2s}\) apart, then \(G\) has chromatic number 4. Along the way, we obtain a few results on the chromatic numbers of certain Euclidean distance graphs having vertex set \(\mathbb Z^3\), the 3-dimensional integer space. We conclude by constructing an example (possibly the first) of a triangle-free, 4-chromatic distance graph in \(\mathbb Q^3\).

hits.title: Two theorems concerning the Babai numbers
On distance graphs in rational spaces
hits.source: Mosc. J. Comb. Number Theory 12, No. 2, 165-173 (2023).
hits.text: Let \(Q_n\) be the set of all positive definite rational quadratic forms on \(n\) variables. For any \(q\in Q_n\), let \(G(Q_n, q)\) denote the graph with vertex set \(Q_n\). Two vertices \(x, y \in Q_n\) are adjacent in the graph if and only if \(q(x - y) = 1\). This notion generalises standard Euclidean distance graphs. In this paper, the authors study these graphs and show how to find the exact value of the clique number of the graph \(G(Q_n, q)\). They also prove a rational analogue of the Beckman-Quarles theorem that any unit-preserving bijection of \(Q_n\) onto itself is an isometry.

hits.title: More on the second Babai number and second clique number of \(\mathbb Q^3\)
hits.text: Let \({\mathbb{Q}}^3 \) be the three-dimensional rational space. In graph \(G({\mathbb{Q}}^3,\{d_1,d_2\})\) two vertices are adjacent if their Euclidean distance is equal to \(d_1\) or \(d_2\) where \(d_1\) and \(d_2\) are positive real numbers. The maximal chromatic number of \(G({\mathbb{Q}}^3,\{d_1,d_2\})\) is called the second Babai number and denoted as \(B_2({\mathbb{Q}}^3)\). The second clique number is the maximal clique number of \(G({\mathbb{Q}}^3,\{d_1,d_2\})\) and denoted as \(C_2({\mathbb{Q}}^3)\). In the paper it is proved that \(C_2({\mathbb{Q}}^3) = 6\) and \(B_2({\mathbb{Q}}^3) \geq 6\).

hits.title: \(C_4\)-factorizations with two associate classes, \(\lambda_1\) is odd
hits.text:
Summary: Let \(K= K(a,p;\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\) be the multigraph with: the number of vertices in each part equal to \(a\); the number of parts equal to \(p\); the number of edges joining any two vertices of the same part equal to \(\lambda_1\); and the number of edges joining any two vertices of different parts equal to \(\lambda_2\). This graph was of interest to \textit{R. C. Bose} and \textit{T. Shimamoto} [J. Am. Stat. Assoc. 47, 151--184 (1952; Zbl 0048.11603)] in their study of group divisible designs with two associate classes.

 Necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of \(z\)-cycle decompositions of this graph have been found when \(z\in\{3; 4\}\). The existence of \(C_4\)-factorizations of \(K\) has been settled when \(a\) is even, and when \(a\equiv 1\pmod 4\) and \(\lambda_1\) is even. In this paper, necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a \(C_4\)-factorization of \(K(a,p;\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\) are found when \(a\equiv 1\pmod 4\) and \(\lambda_1\) is odd with one possible exception.

hits.title: Professional database design with Access
hits.text:
Mit Microsoft ACCESS können Sie alle wichtigen Merkmale relationaler Datenbanken realisieren. So lassen sich beliebige Datenmerkmale zum Auffinden von einzelnen oder Gruppen von Datensätzen nutzen. Dabei ist es möglich, unabhängig voneinander existierende Tabellen mit Hilfe gemeinsamer Merkmale zu verknüpfen.


Das vorliegende Buch geht von einer konkreten, praxiserprobten Anwendungslösung aus, die mit ACCESS entwickelt wird. Am Beispiel einer Personaldatenbank lernen Sie alle Schritte kennen, um mit ACCESS eine umfassende Praxislösung realisieren zu können: Tabellen anlegen und verknüpfen, Formulare zur Datenverwaltung und Menüsteuerung erzeugen, Abfragen gezielt vornehmen, Berichte professionell erstellen und Datenaustausch organisieren.


Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt ist das Programmieren der Anwendungslösung: Gezeigt wird, wie Sie mit ACCESS eine komplette Ablaufsteuerung über Schaltflächen und Menüs organisieren können. Darüber hinaus lernen Sie wichtige Makros in das Programm einbinden. Schließlich wird an ausgewählten Beispielen mit der Programmiersprache Visual BASIC gearbeitet; erzeugte Module werden dann in die Anwendungslösung integriert.


Durch das gezielte, an einem konkreten Fallbeispiel orientierte Vorgehen gewinnen Sie einen schnellen und sicheren Einstieg in die faszinierende Welt der Datenbankentwicklung, der Makros und der Datenbankprogrammierung mit VBA. Dabei wurde versucht die Darstellung möglichst plattformübergreifend zu realisieren, d.h. die Lösungen sind sowohl in der Welt von Windows 95 und Nachfolgeprodukten als auch in der Windows NT-Welt (z.B. für Version 4.0) nutzbar.

hits.title: \(C_4\)-factorizations with two associate classes
hits.text:
Let \(K=K(a,p;\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\) be the multigraph with \(ap\) vertices divided into \(p\) \ parts of size \(a\) \ each, where the number of edges between any two vertices in the same part is \(\lambda_1\) and the number of edges between any two vertices in different parts is \(\lambda_2\). Necessary and sufficient conditions for \(3\)- and \(4\)-cycle decompositions of \(K\) were given in [\textit{H. L. Fu, C. A. Rodger} and \textit{D. G. Sarvate}, Ars Comb. 54, 33--50 (2000; Zbl 0993.05018); \textit{H. L. Fu} and \textit{C. A. Rodger}, Comb. Probab. Comput. 10, 317--343 (2001; Zbl 0992.05030)]. The existence of resolvable \(4\)-cycle decompositions was settled for \(a\) even [\textit{E. J. Billington} and \textit{C. A. Rodger}, Discrete Math. 308, No. 2--3, 303--307 (2008; Zbl 1149.05041)]. 

It is shown that the necessary conditions for the existence of \(C_4\) factorization (i.e., resolvable decomposition) of \(K\) are \(p\equiv0\pmod4, \lambda_2\equiv0\pmod2\), and \(\lambda_2>0\). For \(a\equiv1\pmod4\) also \(\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2 a(p-1)\) must be satisfied. It is proved that these conditions are sufficient when \(a\equiv1\pmod4\) and \(\lambda_1\) is even. For \(a\equiv1\pmod4\) and \(\lambda_1\) odd the existence is proved for \(\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2 a(p-1)-a\).

hits.title: Compactness properties of locally compact groups
hits.text: For a discrete group \(\Gamma\) and an integer \(n\), finiteness properties \(FP_n\) and \(F_n\) are considered. They are defined as follows: \(\Gamma\) is of type \(FP_n\) if there is a projective resolution of \(\mathbb{Z} \Gamma\) over the trivial \(\mathbb{Z} \Gamma\)-module \(\mathbb{Z}\) with finitely generated modules in dimension \(\leq n\). \(\Gamma\) is of type \(F_n\) if there is an Eilenberg-MacLane space \(K (\Gamma,1)\) with finite \(n\)-skeleton. In the paper under review, the authors introduce, as a generalization, compactness properties \(CP_n\) and \(C_n\) for a locally compact group \(G\). They show that, as in the discrete case, \(C_1\) is equivalent to compact generation and \(C_2\) is equivalent to compact presentability. Moreover, it is proved that the compactness properties are preserved by some operations as passing to a cocompact subgroup or to the quotient by a compact normal subgroup.

hits.text: Summary: Let \(K = K(a, p; \lambda_1, \lambda_2)\) be the multigraph with: the number of parts equal to \(p\); the number of vertices in each part equal to \(a\); the number of edges joining any two vertices of the same part equal to \(\lambda_1\); and the number of edges joining any two vertices of different parts equal to \(\lambda_2\). hits.title: \(C_4\)-frames of \(M(b,n)\)
hits.text: Summary: Let \(M (b, n)\) be the complete multipartie graph with \(b\) parts \(B_0, \dots, B_{b-1}\) of size \(n\). A 4-cycle system of \(M (b,n)\) is said to be a frame if the 4-cycles can be partitioned into sets \(S_1, \dots, S_z\) such that for \(1 \leq j \leq z\), \(S_j\) induces a 2-factor of \(M(b, n)\setminus B_i\) for some \(i \in \mathbb Z_b\). The existence of a \(C_4\)-frame of \(M(b, n)\) has been settled when \(n = 4\) [\textit{C. A. Rodger} and \textit{M. A. Tiemeyer}, Australas. J. Comb. 50, 259--278 (2011; Zbl 1236.05165)]. In this paper, we completely settle the existence question of a \(C_4\)-frame of \(M(b, n)\) for all \(b \not= 2\) and \(n\).

Summary: Let \(K= K(a,p; \lambda_1,\lambda_2)\) be the multigraph with: the number of vertices in each part equal to \(a\); the number of parts equal to \(p\); the number of edges joining any two vertices of the same part equal to \(\lambda_1\); and the number of edges joining any two vertices of different parts equal to \(\lambda_2\). hits.title: On cycle frames with cycles of length 8
hits.text:
Summary: Let \(M(b,n)\) be the complete multipartite graph with \(b\) parts \(B_0,\dots, B_{b-1}\) of size \(n\). A \(z\)-cycle system of \(M(b,n)\) is said to be a cycle-frame if the \(z\)-cycles can be partitioned into sets \(S_1,\dots, S_k\) such that for \(1\leq j\leq k\), \(S_j\) induces a 2-factor of \(M(b,n)\setminus B_i\) for some \(i\in\mathbb{Z}_i\). The existence of a \(C_z\)-frame of \(M(b,n)\) has been settled when \(z\in\{3,4,5,6\}\).

 Here, we completely settle the case of \(C_z\)-frames when \(z\) is 8, and we give some solutions for larger values of \(z\).

hits.title: Which pairs of distances can be forbidden by a 4-coloring of \(Q\)?
A local-global principle for finiteness properties of \(S\)-arithmetic groups over number fields
hits.text: The main object of the paper under review is an \(S\)-arithmetic subgroup \(\Gamma\) of a linear algebraic group \(G\) defined over a number field. The goal is to establish a local-global principle for some finiteness properties of \(\Gamma\) by relating them to compactness properties of \(p\)-adic completions \(G_p\) studied by \textit{H. Abels} and \textit{A. Tiemeyer} [Transform. Groups 2, No. 2, 119-135 (1997)]. This gives an alternative proof of finiteness theorems by \textit{A. Borel} and \textit{J.-P. Serre} [Topology 15, 211-232 (1976; Zbl 0338.20055)]\ (for \(G\) reductive) and P. Abramenko (for \(P\) a parabolic subgroup of \(G\)).

hits.title: Compactness properties of locally compact groups
hits.source: Bielefeld: Fak. f. Math., Univ. Bielefeld, 40 S. (1994).
hits.text:
In this very interesting and clearly written thesis the author defines compactness conditions \(CP_n\) and \(C_n\) for an arbitrary locally compact group \(G\) as follows. The classifying space \(EG\) of \(G\) has a natural invariant filtration \(\underline A\), and \(G\) is said to be of type \(CP_n\) (resp. \(C_n)\) if all homology groups \(H_i (\underline A) = 0\) (resp. all homotopy groups \(\pi_i (\underline A) = 0)\) for all \(i < n\). In the case of discrete groups, these notions coincide with the finiteness conditions \(FP_n\) and \(F_n\) previously considered in the literature [see \textit{K. S. Brown}, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 44, 45-75 (1987; Zbl 0613.20033)]. It is shown that \(G\) being of type \(C_1\) is equivalent with \(G\) being compactly generated and that \(G\) being of type \(C_2\) is equivalent with \(G\) being compactly presented. 


The author then establishes a Hasse principle for \(S\)-arithmetic subgroups \(\Gamma\) of an algebraic group \(G\): \(\Gamma\) is of type \(F_n\) if and only if \(G_p\) is of type \(C_n\) for all non-archimedean places \(p\) in \(S\). This allows him to give a simpler proof of a result by \textit{A. Borel} and \textit{J.-P. Serre} [Topology 15, 211-232 (1976; Zbl 0338.20055)] to the effect that an \(S\)-arithmetic subgroup of a reductive algebraic group is of type \(F_\infty\) (that is, it has all finiteness properties). Moreover, it is shown that a real Lie group with finitely many components is of type \(C_\infty\).

hits.title: A very short proof of a well-known fact about circles in the plane
hits.text: Summary: The fact referred to in the title is that if \(C\) is a circle in the coordinatized real plane centered at a rational point and containing a rational point, then the rational points are dense on \(C\). From one well-known proof of this fact it can be deduced that for any two such circles, there is a homeomorphism of one onto the other that takes the rational points of the domain onto those of the range. From our proof it is obvious that there is such a correspondence arising from the composition of an isometry and a homothethic transformation of the plane.

hits.title: An isomorphism problem in $\mathbb Z^2$
hits.source: Theory Appl. Graphs 2, No. 1, Article 1, 8 p. (2015).
hits.text: Summary: We consider Euclidean distance graphs with vertex set $\mathbb Q^2$ or $\mathbb Z^2$ and address the possibility or impossibility of finding isomorphisms between such graphs. It is observed that for any distances $d_1,d_2$ the non-trivial (that is, having non-empty edge set) distance graphs $G(\mathbb Q^2,d_1)$ and $G(\mathbb Q^2,d_2)$ are isomorphic. Ultimately it is shown that for distinct primes $p_1,p_2$ the non-trivial distance graphs $G(\mathbb Z^2,\sqrt{p_1})$ and $G(\mathbb Z^2,\sqrt{p_2})$ are not isomorphic. We conclude with a few additional questions related to this work.

hits.title: On 4-chromatic subgraphs of \(G(\mathbb Q^3,d)\)
hits.text: Summary: We address the chromatic number of a class of Euclidean distance graphs having vertex set \(\mathbb Q^3\), the 3-dimensional rational space. It is shown that if \(s\) is any positive integer with no prime factors congruent to \(2\pmod{3}\), and \(G\) is the graph with vertex set \(\mathbb Q^3\) where any two vertices are adjacent if and only if they are distance \(\sqrt{2s}\) apart, then \(G\) has chromatic number 4. Along the way, we obtain a few results on the chromatic numbers of certain Euclidean distance graphs having vertex set \(\mathbb Z^3\), the 3-dimensional integer space. We conclude by constructing an example (possibly the first) of a triangle-free, 4-chromatic distance graph in \(\mathbb Q^3\).

hits.title: Application of an extremal result of Erdős and Gallai to the $(n,k,t)$ problem
hits.source: Theory Appl. Graphs 4, No. 2, Article 1, 5 p. (2017).
hits.text: Summary: An extremal result about vertex covers, attributed by \textit{Hajnal} [Can. J. Math. 17, 720--724 (1965; Zbl 0129.39901)] to \textit{P. Erdős} and \textit{T. Gallai} [Publ. Math. Inst. Hung. Acad. Sci., Ser. A 6, 181--203 (1961; Zbl 0101.41001)], is applied to prove the following: If $n$, $k$, and $t$ are integers satisfying $n\ge k\ge t\ge 3$ and $k\le 2t-2$, and $G$ is a graph with the minimum number of edges among graphs on $n$ vertices with the property that every induced subgraph on $k$ vertices contains a complete subgraph on $t$ vertices, then every component of $G$ is complete.

hits.title: Isosceles triangles in \(\mathbb Q^3\)
hits.text:
Summary: In this article, we give a characterization of isosceles triangles having as their vertices points of the rational Euclidean space \(\mathbb{Q}^3\). For positive integers \(d\) and \(r\) where \(\sqrt{d}\) and \(\sqrt{r}\) are both realized as distances in \(\mathbb{Q}^3\) and \(r= a^2+ b^2+ c^2\) for integers \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), it is shown that the triangle with edges of length \(\sqrt{d}\), \(\sqrt{d}\), and \(\sqrt{r}\) is embeddable in \(\mathbb{Q}^3\) if and only if the Diophantine equation \(x^2+ ry^2- (4d-r) (a^2+ b^2)z^2=0\) has a non-trivial integer solution. This condition is used to give new proofs of a few recent results concerning \(G(\mathbb{Q}^3,\sqrt{r})\), the Euclidean distance graph with vertex set \(\mathbb{Q}^3\) where adjacent vertices are at distance \(\sqrt{r}\) apart.

Originally shown by \textit{E. J. Ionascu} [Acta Math. Univ. Comen., New Ser. 77, No. 1, 129--140 (2008; Zbl 1164.11016)], we prove that \(G(\mathbb{Q}^3,\sqrt{r})\) contains \(K_3\) as a subgraph if and only if the square-free part of \(r\) is even but has no odd factor congruent to \((\mathrm{mod}\ 3)\). We conclude by proving that each of those graphs \(G(\mathbb{Q}^3,\sqrt{r})\) which contain \(K_3\) as a subgraph have chromatic number \(4\).

hits.title: Proper rainbow-cycle-forbidding edge colorings of graphs
hits.text:
Summary: It is well known that if the edges of a finite simple graph on \(n\) vertices are colored so that no cycle is rainbow, then no more than \(n-1\) colors may appear on the edges. In previous work it was shown that a certain structure theorem held true for edge colorings with exactly \(n-1\) colors appearing in which no cycle is rainbow. In this paper we consider edge colorings which are proper and ``forbid'' rainbow cycles, without the condition that the maximum number of colors must appear.

Two questions about the eponymous edge colorings are considered: which graphs have such a coloring, and, for a graph \(G\) that does have such a coloring, for what values of \(k\) does \(G\) have a coloring with exactly \(k\) colors appearing?

hits.title: Embedding partial 3-star designs
hits.source: Electron. J. Graph Theory Appl. 12, No. 2, 289-295 (2024).
hits.text: Summary: Define a 3-star decomposition of \(K_n\) as being a collection of subgraphs, each isomorphic to \(K_{1,3}\), with the property that each edge of \(K_n\) appears in exactly one of the subgraphs. A partial 3-star decomposition is similarly defined except each edge appears in at most one of the subgraphs. In this work, it is shown that any partial 3-star decomposition of \(K_n\) can be embedded into a decomposition of \(K_{n+s}\) where \(s \leq 4\). Furthermore, we determine, for any maximal partial 3-star decomposition \(\mathscr{P}\) of \(K_n\), the minimum \(s \in \{1,2,3,4\}\) such that \(\mathscr{P}\) can be embedded into a decomposition of \(K_{n+s}\).

hits.title: Assorted musings on dimension-critical graphs
hits.text: Summary: Let \(G\) be a finite simple graph. We say \(G\) is of dimension \(n\), writing \(\dim(G)=n\), if \(n\) is the smallest integer such that \(G\) can be represented as a unit-distance graph in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Define \(G\) to be dimension-critical if every proper subgraph of \(G\) has dimension less than \(G\). In this article, we determine exactly which complete multipartite graphs are dimension-critical. It is then shown that for each \(n\geq 2\), there is an arbitrarily large dimension-critical graph \(G\) with \(\dim(G)=n\). We then pose and expound upon a number of questions related to this subject matter.

hits.title: Answer to an isomorphism problem in \(\mathbb{Z}^2\)
hits.text: Summary: For \(S\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(d>0\), denote by \(G(S,d)\) the graph with vertex set \(S\) with any two vertices being adjacent if and only if they are at an Euclidean distance \(d\) apart. Deem such a graph to be ``non-trivial'' if \(d\) is actually realized as a distance between points of \(S\). The author [Theory Appl. Graphs 2, No. 1, Article 1, 8 p. (2015; Zbl 1416.05095)] asked if there exist distinct \(d_1\), \(d_2\) such that the non-trivial graphs \(G(\mathbb{Z}^2,d_1)\) and \(G(\mathbb{Z}^2,d_2)\) are isomorphic. In our current work, we offer a straightforward geometric construction to show that a negative answer holds for this question.

hits.title: On rainbow cycles and proper edge colorings of generalized polygons
hits.source: Theory Appl. Graphs 10, No. 1, Article 2, 9 p. (2023).
hits.text: A proper rainbow-cycle-forbidding edge-coloring of a graph \(G\) is a proper edge-coloring such that on every cycle of \(G\) at least two edges are colored with the same color. A graph is PRCF-good if it admits such coloring and PRCF-bad otherwise. Clearly, no graph with a triangle is PRCF-good, but it is not clear whether there exist PRCF-bad graphs with large girths. While in previous works PRCF-bad graphs of girth \(4\) have been introduced, the author of this paper elegantly shows that the Hoffman-Singleton graph (which has girth \(5\)) is also PRCF-bad. Moreover, using a similar counting argument, he shows that there are generalized polygons of girths \(6\), \(8\), \(12\), and \(16\) which are also PRCF-bad. It remains an open question whether there are PRCF-bad graphs of large girth and also whether there is an infinite family of graphs with some chosen girth (at least \(5\)) that are PRCF-bad.

hits.title: Isomorphism classes of distance graphs in \(\mathbb{Q}^3\)
hits.text: Summary: For \(d > 0\), designate by \(G(\mathbb{Q}^3, d)\) the graph whose set of vertices is the rational space \(\mathbb{Q}^3\), with any two vertices being adjacent if and only if they are Euclidean distance \(d\) apart. Deem such a graph to be ``non-trivial'' if \(d\) is actually realized as a distance between points of \(\mathbb{Q}^3\). In this work, we prove that non-trivial graphs \(G(\mathbb{Q}^3,d_1)\) and \(G(\mathbb{Q}^3, d^2)\) are isomorphic if and only if \(d_1\), \(d_2\) are rational multiples of each other. This determination of the isomorphism classes of graphs with vertex set \(\mathbb{Q}^3\) answers a question posed by \textit{P. Johnson} [Prog. Math. 285, 163--176 (2011; Zbl 1243.05082)].

hits.title: Dimension 4 and dimension 5 graphs with minimum edge set
hits.text: Summary: The dimension of a graph \(G\) is defined to be the minimum \(n\) such that \(G\) has a representation as a unit-distance graph in \(\mathbb R^n\). A problem posed by P. Erdős [\textit{P. Erdős} et al., Mathematika, Lond. 12, 118--122 (1965; Zbl 0151.33204)] asks for the minimum number of edges in a graph of dimension 4. In a recent article, \textit{R. F. House} [Discrete Math. 313, No. 18, 1783--1789 (2013; Zbl 1277.05088)] showed that the answer to Erdős' question is 9. In this article, we give a shorter (and we feel more straightforward) proof of House's result, and then extend our methods to answer the question for dimension 5 as well. It is ultimately shown that a dimension 5 graph has at least 15 edges, and that this lower bound is realized only by two graphs: \(K_6\) and \(K_{1,3,3}\).

hits.title: Odd vector cycles in \(\mathbb{Z}^m\)
hits.text: Summary: Given positive integers \(m\) and \(r\), define \(C_m(r)\) to be the minimum odd number of \(\mathbb{Z}^m\) vectors, each of magnitude \(\sqrt{r}\), that together sum to the zero vector. In this article, \(C_m(r)\) is investigated for various assignments of \(m\) and \(r\). A few previous results are combined to definitively answer the question except in the case of \(m= 3\) and the square-free part of \(r\) being even and also containing at least one odd prime factor \(x\) with \(x\equiv 2 \pmod 3\). We detail the results of a computer-assisted search to determine \(C_3(r)\) for all \(r <10^6\) and then discuss parameterizations of vector cycles in \(\mathbb{Z}^3\) of length five. We close with a few conjectures and open questions.

hits.title: Chromatic numbers of two-distance graphs in \(\mathbb Q^2\)
hits.text: Given a metric space \((X,\rho)\) and a distance set \(D\), one can construct a distance graph \(G(X,D)\) in such a way that \(V(G)=X\) and \(E(G)=\{\{x,y\}|x,y\in X,\rho(x,y)\in D\}\). hits.title: $\gamma'$-realizability and other Musings on inverse domination
hits.source: Theory Appl. Graphs 5, No. 1, Article 5, 7 p. (2018).
hits.text: Summary: We introduce and study $\gamma^\prime$-realizable sequences. For a finite, simple graph $G$ containing no isolated vertices, $I\subseteq V(G)$ is said to be an inverse dominating set if $I$ dominates $G$ and $I$ is contained by the complement of some minimum dominating set $D$. Define a sequence of positive integers $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ to be $\gamma^\prime$-realizable if there exists a graph $G$ having exactly $n$ distinct minimum dominating sets $D_1,\dots,D_n$ where for each $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, the minimum size of an inverse dominating set in $V(G)\setminus D_i$ is equal to $x_i$. In this work, we show which sequences having minimum entry 2 or less are $\gamma^\prime$-realizable. We then detail a few observations and results arising during our investigations that may prove useful in future research.

hits.title: Problems on the Triangular Lattice
hits.text: Summary: In this work, we consider a number of problems defined on the triangular lattice with $n$ rows, which we will denote as $T_n$. Define a \textit{proper coloring} to be an assignment of colors to the points of $T_n$ such that no three points constituting the vertices of an equilateral triangle all receive the same color, and denote by $f(n)$ the smallest possible number of colors that can be used in a proper coloring of $T_n$. We either determine exactly or give upper bounds for $f(n)$ for many small values of $n$, and it is shown that $\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{f(n)}{n} \leq \frac13$. We also give formulas counting the number of pairs of points in $T_n$ for which there are, respectively, 0, 1, or 2 choices of points in $T_n$ which extend those two into the vertices of an equilateral triangle. Along the way, we pose a number of related questions.

hits.title: A very short proof of a well-known fact about circles in the plane
hits.text: Summary: The fact referred to in the title is that if \(C\) is a circle in the coordinatized real plane centered at a rational point and containing a rational point, then the rational points are dense on \(C\). From one well-known proof of this fact it can be deduced that for any two such circles, there is a homeomorphism of one onto the other that takes the rational points of the domain onto those of the range. From our proof it is obvious that there is such a correspondence arising from the composition of an isometry and a homothethic transformation of the plane.

hits.title: On the chromatic number of real and rational spaces
hits.text:
Summary: The chromatic number of a space is the minimum number of colors with which the whole space can be colored so that no two points of the same color are at unit distance.

We prove that the chromatic number of the six-dimensional real Euclidean space, \(\mathbb R^6\), is at least 11. In addition we give a new proof of the lower bound 9 for the chromatic number of \(\mathbb R^5\). We also simplify the proof of the lower bound 7 for \(\mathbb R^4\).

We improve the lower bounds on the chromatic number of five-dimensional and seven-dimensional rational space to 8 and 15, respectively.

hits.title: Rational trigonometry: computational viewpoint
hits.text: In the book of [\textit{N. J. Wildberger}, Divine Proportions: Rational Trigonometry to Universal Geometry. (Kingsford): Wild Egg. (2005; Zbl 1192.00004)] it is shown that if we characterize each side \(a_{i}\) of a triangle by its ``quadrance'' \( s_{i}:=a_{i}^{2}\) and each angle \(A_{i}\)\ by its ``spread'' \(Q_{i}:=\sin ^{2}(A_{i}),\) then all the formulas for solving triangles become algebraic. Formulas using \(s_{i}\) and \(Q_{i}\) are called rational trigonometry. The author shows that rational trigonometry is the computationally fastest way of solving triangles.

hits.title: Imaginary coloring
hits.text: Shelah and Soifer found a simple graph for which the chromatic number is not uniquely determined by Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory ZF. This graph has as underlying set the real numbers and there is an edge between \(x\) and \(y\) if and only if \(x-y\) is the sum of a rational number and \(\sqrt 2\). Assuming AC (axiom of choice) the chromatic number of this graph is two whereas DP+LM (dependent choice and ``every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable'') implies that the chromatic number is uncountable. In this paper the authors give a historical and philosophical view of this result and explain the proof given by Shelah and Soifer.

hits.title: Unit distance subgraphs of critical graphs
hits.text: This paper discusses the realizations of chromatically-critical graphs containing many edges of unit length. This paper proves that for any rational number \(q\) between \(\frac{5}{3}\) and \(\frac{9}{5}\), there exists a \(4\)-critical plane graph \(G\) having a faithful unit-distance drawing and \(\frac{E(G)}{V(G)}=q\). A construction of infinite sequences of 5-, 6-, and 7-critical graphs containing large unit distance subgraphs is done.

In graph \(G({\mathbb{Q}}^3,\{d_1,d_2\})\) two vertices are adjacent if their Euclidean distance is equal to \(d_1\) or \(d_2\) where \(d_1\) and \(d_2\) are positive real numbers. hits.title: Rigid colorings of hypergraphs and contiguity
hits.text: Summary: We consider the problem of \(q\)-coloring a \(k\)-uniform random hypergraph, where \(q,k \geq 3\), and determine the rigidity threshold. For edge densities above the rigidity threshold, we show that almost all solutions have a linear number of vertices that are linearly frozen, meaning that they cannot be recolored by a sequence of colorings that each change the color of a sublinear number of vertices. When the edge density is below the threshold, we prove that all but a vanishing proportion of the vertices can be recolored by a sequence of colorings that recolor only one vertex at a time. This change in the geometry of the solution space has been hypothesized to be the cause of the algorithmic barrier faced by naive coloring algorithms. Our calculations verify predictions made by statistical physicists using the nonrigorous cavity method. The traditional model for problems of this type is the random coloring model, where a random hypergraph is chosen and then a random coloring of that hypergraph is selected. However, it is often easier to work with the planted model, where a random coloring is selected first, and then edges are randomly chosen which respect the coloring. As part of our analysis, we show that up to the condensation phase transition, the random coloring model is contiguous with respect to the planted model. This result is of independent interest.
